body: Denver-based Four Mile Capital bought River's Edge, a 10-story, 212-unit apartment building at 505 Porter St. in Richmond's Manchester area, in 2021 for $47.5 million, Richmond BizSense reported. Four Mile sued the development team, Reynolds South Tower LLC, which includes principals of CMB Development and Purcell Construction Corp., in Richmond Circuit Court in May 2025. The suit alleges three counts of fraud, breach of contract, negligence and business conspiracy, and seeks more than $40 million and a jury trial.

Four Mile says it knew of leaks before the sale and that the sellers agreed to make repairs before and after closing, but that Purcell refused further repairs in 2022. In 2023, a firm Four Mile hired reportedly found the building was 'not built in accordance with its design' and lacked waterproof sheathing Four Mile says it was told was there. Four Mile says the facade must be reclad at a cost of millions, requiring tenants to relocate.

At an August 7, 2026 hearing, the defense sought dismissal of the fraud counts. Reynolds South argued Four Mile was not misled, had time for further inspections and accepted the repair work in writing before closing, and Purcell said it fulfilled its contractual responsibilities. In a September 21 opinion, McClenney largely denied the demurrer but sustained it on certain counts against Purcell, finding it was not a party to the sale and not contractually bound to Four Mile, BizSense reported on October 21. Four Mile amended its complaint on October 13 to drop Purcell from the breach of contract claim. Four Mile's attorney called the ruling a win; the defendants have denied wrongdoing, and no trial date has been set.
